subject: ela
intro: Analyze text structure and section function.

items.prompt:
A text organized by dates from 1900 to 2000 uses:
A) chronological structure
B) compare and contrast
C) problem and solution

Headings in a text help the reader:
A) know what each section is about
B) count words
C) pick a font
items.answer: A) know what each section is about

steps: Guide the reader. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) know what each section is about

items.prompt:
'Because' and 'as a result' signal:
A) cause and effect
B) chronology only
C) comparison

Read.

Section 1: the problem of plastic pollution. Section 2: its causes. Section 3: solutions.

The overall structure is:
A) problem and solution
B) pure chronology
C) compare and contrast

steps: Problem, causes, solutions. Key is A.

items.prompt:
In that text, the 'solutions' section contributes by:
A) responding to the problem raised earlier
B) starting a new topic
C) listing the author's hobbies
items.answer: A) responding to the problem raised earlier

steps: Completes the argument. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) responding to the problem raised earlier

items.prompt:
A text that asks 'Why do volcanoes erupt?' and then answers it uses:
A) question and answer structure
B) compare and contrast
C) chronology

steps: Q then A. Key is A.

items.prompt:
An author organizes an article as: history of the disease, then current treatments, then future research. The structure is BEST described as:
A) chronological (past, present, future)
B) compare and contrast
C) problem and solution only

steps: Organized by time. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Why do authors divide informational texts into labeled SECTIONS?
A) so each part develops the ideas and contributes to the whole
B) to hide information
C) to make the text random
items.answer: A) so each part develops the ideas and contributes to the whole

steps: Sections build the whole. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) so each part develops the ideas and contributes to the whole
